rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for saying that someone or something is across from a reference point.

example.english: Your office is opposite, so it’s easy for me to walk over.
example.traditional: 你公司喺對面，我行過嚟好方便。
example.jyutping: nei5 gung1 si1 hai2 deoi3 min6 ngo5 haang4 gwo3 lei4 hou2 fong1 bin6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose way to say that something is across from a place or object.

example.english: The cha chaan teng is opposite the cinema.
example.jyutping: caa4 gei3 hai2 hei3 jyun2 deoi3 min6

rows.note: Use this when one place or object directly faces another, rather than simply being across from it.

example.english: This shop is opposite the MTR station.
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 pou3 deoi3 zyu6 dei6 tit3 zaam6

rows.traditional: 同 A 相反嘅 B
rows.jyutping: tung4 A soeng1 faan2 ge3 B
rows.note: This is the all-purpose pattern for a person or thing that is substantively different from A.

example.english: He is the opposite of me.
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai6 tung4 ngo5 soeng1 faan2 ge3 jan4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for things that are contrary or extremely different.

example.english: Their two opinions are completely opposite.
example.traditional: 佢哋兩個嘅諗法完全相反。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 ge3 nam2 faat3 jyun4 cyun4 soeng1 faan2

rows.note: Use this for a place or person located directly across from something else.

example.english: The bus stop is opposite the school.
example.jyutping: baa1 si2 zaam6 hai2 hok6 haau6 deoi3 min6

rows.note: Use this specifically for a word with the opposite meaning, such as “up” versus “down.”

example.jyutping: soeng6 ge3 faan2 ji6 ci4 hai6 lok6

rows.note: Use this specifically for movement or facing in the other direction.

example.english: We walk away in opposite directions.
example.traditional: 我哋向住相反方向行開。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 hoeng3 zyu6 soeng1 faan2 fong1 hoeng3 haang4 hoi1

rows.note: Use this for someone you compete or fight against.

example.english: Our opponent in this match is last year's champion, the opposite of a pushover.
example.traditional: 我哋今場嘅對手係上屆冠軍。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 coeng4 ge3 deoi3 sau2 hai6 soeng6 gaai3 gun3 gwan1

rows.jyutping: tung4 A zou6 deoi3 sau2 hei3
rows.note: Use this when describing an actor performing scenes with a named co-star.

example.english: This time I’m acting opposite Nick Cheung.
example.traditional: 我今次同張家輝做對手戲。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 ci3 tung4 zoeng1 gaa1 fai1 zou6 deoi3 sau2 hei3

rows.note: Use this for the other one of two alternatives or complementary things.

example.english: You take this one, and I’ll take the opposite one.
example.jyutping: nei5 gaan2 ni1 go3 ngo5 gaan2 ling6 jat1 go3

rows.note: Use this for the other party or counterpart in an interaction, especially when the relationship is not necessarily hostile.

example.english: The opposite party has already agreed to deliver the goods on Friday.
example.traditional: 對方已經答應星期五交貨。
example.jyutping: deoi3 fong1 ji5 ging1 daap3 jing3 sing1 kei4 ng5 gaau1 fo3
